page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-8GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, vector neural network instructions (AVX512_VNNI), and SHA extensions.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is in the top tier (top 10%), and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong (top 25%). However, because of the shared CPU allocation, multi-core performance scales down, with Geekbench multi-core scores and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the weak category (bottom 25%). Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is weak, though large block read and write bandwidths remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation and lack of bundled local storage position this instance as a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated multi-core execution. It is suited for static web serving, where it achieves average throughput, and basic text processing tasks. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or heavy multi-threaded processing due to lower multi-core efficiency and weak Redis SET performance.
